cards.name: PS Arbitrary Map

verified.note: Phase 180 now wraps the tones hard (solarize-like): mid-dark tones (luma 64-127) jump to near-white so the navy areas turn white, highlights (luma 160+) drop to dark so faces and backdrop go grey-black, reds flip to cyan with posterized colour fringes, where the old Phase-0 render was identical to the reference (mean change 127/255 vs 0).
verified.second_opinion: corrected: verdict broken and status obsolete confirmed (051 differs from the Bulge frame 060 by 0.13 mean outside the bulge radius, so no tone change), but 'no demo setting can fix it' is wrong: demo_settings {} is the no-op cause. Phase has no harvested min/max like every AE angle param (CC Color Offset Red Phase, Evolution, Direction), so it is degrees, and AE applies the default linear map when none is loaded; demo set to Phase 180 (half-cycle tone wrap) and queued for re-render, Phase/scripting/avoid notes updated

cards.summary: Legacy effect that remaps the layer's brightness/colour through a Photoshop arbitrary map (.amp curve file) loaded in the effect's Options dialog; Phase cycles the map along the tone range. Curves does the same job today.
use_for: keeping old projects that already carry a Photoshop .amp map rendering the same
psychedelic tone-cycling by animating Phase on a loaded map
avoid: any new grade: use Curves or Lumetri Color instead

a script cannot load the .amp file: a freshly applied instance at Phase 0 renders identical to the source; only a non-zero Phase on the default linear map changes it (verified: Phase 180 = harsh solarize-like wrap, gallery frame 051)

params.name: Phase
params.does: shifts (cycles) the loaded map along the tone range
params.typical: angle in degrees (unbounded, like all AE angle params): 360 = one full cycle = no change; 180 wraps the tones half-way (solarize-like); animate 0 -> 360 for tone cycling

params.name: Apply Phase Map To Alpha
params.does: checkbox: also run the map on the alpha channel

cards.equivalent: AE replacement: Curves (ADBE CurvesCustom); Premiere: Lumetri Color RGB Curves
cards.scripting: The map itself is not a scriptable property: it lives in the Options dialog (load a Photoshop .amp file). Applied by script it keeps the default linear (identity) map, which leaves the image unchanged (verified: Phase 0 renders identical to the source). Phase cycles that map; it has no harvested min/max, which in AE means an angle param, so it is in degrees (360 = full cycle); a non-zero Phase wraps the tones (verified: Phase 180 sends mid-darks to near-white and highlights to dark, reds to cyan, with posterized edges, gallery frame 051). Both properties are animatable. Treat as obsolete: build tone remaps with Curves. Apply Phase Map To Alpha is a 0/1 checkbox.

cards.name: Photo Filter

verified.note: Clear warm amber cast over the whole frame (R up, B down) with brightness held, as Warming Filter (85) at Density 65 should give.

cards.summary: Simulates a coloured lens filter: casts the image toward a warming, cooling or custom colour at a chosen density while keeping brightness.
use_for: warm up flat press/handout footage for a hopeful or nostalgic beat
cool blue cast for tense or investigative documentary sections
quick temperature match between clips from different cameras
light sepia/flashback feel on archival inserts
avoid: Density above ~60 reads as a cheap colour wash
Preserve Luminosity off darkens the shot
not a fix for badly white-balanced faces; use Lumetri/Curves first

params.name: Filter
params.does: preset filter popup; 1 = Warming Filter (85); a Custom entry uses Color
params.typical: 1 Warming Filter (85) for warm; 4 Cooling Filter (80) for blue; 15 Sepia

params.name: Color
params.does: custom filter colour, used when Filter is Custom

params.name: Density
params.does: strength of the filter in percent

params.name: Preserve Luminosity
params.does: checkbox: keep overall brightness after tinting

cards.equivalent: Lumetri Color (Basic Correction Temperature/Tint or Creative Shadow/Highlight Tint) in Premiere
cards.scripting: Filter is a 1-based popup with 22 entries; 1 = Warming Filter (85) (matches the default Color #EC8A00). The rest (read from After Effects 26.0): 2 Warming (LBA), 3 Warming (81), 4 Cooling (80), 5 Cooling (LBB), 6 Cooling (82), 7 Red, 8 Orange, 9 Yellow, 10 Green, 11 Cyan, 12 Blue, 13 Violet, 14 Magenta, 15 Sepia, 16 Deep Red, 17 Deep Blue, 18 Deep Emerald, 19 Deep Yellow, 20 Underwater, 21 a separator, 22 Custom; only index 1 has been rendered. Color only matters with Custom. Preserve Luminosity is a 0/1 checkbox.

cards.name: Selective Color

verified.note: Strong orange-yellow cast through the Neutrals (walls, clothing, skin, even the white stripes), so the scripted proxy sliders on Colors: 8 did stick in the render.

cards.summary: Photoshop-style selective colour: adds or removes cyan, magenta, yellow and black inside one colour range (reds, yellows, greens, cyans, blues, magentas, whites, neutrals, blacks) without touching the others.
use_for: make saffron/red flags and banners richer, or tame over-saturated reds on rally footage
teal-orange look: cyan into Blues/Neutrals, yellow into Reds
remove a green/magenta cast from Neutrals on mixed-light press footage
deeper Blacks for a punchy news look
avoid: big moves on Reds/Yellows wreck skin tones
the top Cyan/Magenta/Yellow/Black sliders are UI proxies (see scripting): they only edit the range picked in 'Colors:', so set that first
Absolute moves of 40+ on Neutrals tint almost the whole frame, whites and skin included

params.name: Method:
params.does: 1 Relative (scales existing ink) or 2 Absolute (adds fixed amount, stronger)

params.name: Colors:
params.does: which colour range the top four sliders edit (1 Reds .. 9 Blacks)

params.name: Cyan
params.does: add (+) or remove (-) cyan in the selected range

params.name: Magenta
params.does: add or remove magenta in the selected range

params.name: Yellow
params.does: add or remove yellow in the selected range

params.name: Black
params.does: darken (+) or lighten (-) the selected range

cards.equivalent: Lumetri Color HSL Secondary / Hue vs Saturation curves in Premiere
cards.scripting: Names repeat: the first Cyan/Magenta/Yellow/Black (match ADBE SelectiveColor-0003..0006) are non-animatable UI proxies that edit the range picked in 'Colors:' - set 'Colors:' BEFORE them (keep that key first in the props object). A scripted setValue on the proxies does reach the render (gallery check: 'Colors:' 8 then Cyan -45 / Magenta 10 / Yellow 50 with Method 2 gave a strong orange cast). The real, animatable values sit flat under 'Details' (headers are flat rows, so 'Reds/Cyan' resolves to the proxy, not the Reds value). To target a range reliably, address by MATCH NAME (AE property() accepts it): Reds 0009-0012, Yellows 0015-0018, Greens 0021-0024, Cyans 0027-0030, Blues 0033-0036, Magentas 0039-0042, Whites 0045-0048, Neutrals 0051-0054, Blacks 0057-0060, each 'ADBE SelectiveColor-00NN' in C, M, Y, K order. The validator only knows display names (the n-th repeat is 'Cyan#n', e.g. Neutrals Cyan = 'Cyan#9'), and ae_lib dress() does not parse '#n', so the demo uses the proxies on Neutrals (8, present in almost every shot: a strong warm cast) rather than Reds (invisible on footage with no red). Animatability (proxies and 'Colors:' static, Details values animatable) is from the harvest.

cards.name: Shadow/Highlight

verified.note: Highlights are pulled down hard (bright walls and faces drop about 30-50 levels, HDR-ish grey look) while the few dark areas stay put, since this evenly lit shot has almost no deep shadows to lift.

cards.summary: Brightens shadows and/or darkens highlights locally, based on surrounding pixels, without flattening the midtones; recovers backlit faces and blown skies.
use_for: lift faces in backlit podium or rally shots
pull back a bright sky or window behind a speaker
rescue underexposed phone or archival news footage
HDR-ish detail look on documentary B-roll
avoid: Shadow Amount above ~60 gives halos and grey, muddy blacks
Highlight Amount ~50 on an evenly lit, bright shot pulls faces and walls down too and greys the whole image; keep it 10-30 there
Auto Amounts on moving shots flickers unless Temporal Smoothing is set
without some contrast afterwards the image looks washed out

params.name: Auto Amounts
params.does: checkbox: automatic amounts; must be 0 for the manual amounts to apply

params.name: Shadow Amount
params.does: how much the shadows are lifted

params.name: Highlight Amount
params.does: how much the highlights are pulled down

params.name: Shadow Radius
params.does: neighbourhood size used to decide what is shadow (bigger = smoother, more halo)

params.name: Midtone Contrast
params.does: adds contrast back into the midtones

params.name: Temporal Smoothing (seconds)
params.does: averages auto amounts over time (only with Auto Amounts on)

params.name: Blend With Original
params.does: mixes the original back in (percent)

cards.equivalent: Lumetri Color Basic Correction Shadows/Highlights in Premiere
cards.scripting: Auto Amounts is a 0/1 checkbox that defaults to 1: Shadow Amount and Highlight Amount are ignored until it is set to 0 (put it first in props). Temporal Smoothing and Scene Detect only matter with Auto Amounts = 1. 'More Options' is a flat header row, so the sub-properties are addressed by plain name.

cards.name: Tint

verified.note: Frame is a navy-to-cream duotone monochrome (all original colour gone), matching the demo's Map Black/White colours.

cards.summary: Turns the layer monochrome by mapping its darks to one colour and its lights to another (black-and-white by default); Amount to Tint blends with the original colour.
use_for: instant black-and-white for flashbacks or archival recreations
brand-colour duotone background plates behind titles
desaturate the background clip under a coloured cut-out of the speaker
partial desaturation (Amount 30-60) for a muted documentary look
avoid: two mid-grey map colours give a flat, low-contrast image
full B&W on colourful rally footage loses the flags' meaning; keep some colour or use it deliberately

params.name: Map Black To
params.does: colour the darkest tones become
params.typical: #000000 for B&W, deep navy #14213D for duotone

params.name: Map White To
params.does: colour the brightest tones become
params.typical: #FFFFFF for B&W, warm cream #FFD58A for duotone

params.name: Amount to Tint
params.does: percent of the tint applied over the original

cards.scripting: Colours are '#RRGGBB'. Amount to Tint (0-100) is animatable: keyframe it for a colour-to-B&W transition. GPU support is from memory, not harvested.

cards.name: Tritone

verified.note: Frame is a brown sepia toned monochrome with cream highlights and near-black shadows, the classic tritone look.

cards.summary: Maps the image's highlights, midtones and shadows to three chosen colours, giving a toned monochrome (sepia by default).
use_for: sepia/vintage look for history segments in documentaries
brand-toned background plates behind text
stylised flashback in trailers
Blend With Original 40-70 for a subtle split-tone grade
avoid: a bright saturated midtone colour looks cheap
removes natural skin tones; avoid where faces must look real

params.name: Highlights
params.does: colour for the bright tones

params.name: Midtones
params.does: colour for the midtones (sets the tone of the look)

params.name: Shadows
params.does: colour for the dark tones

params.name: Blend With Original
params.does: percent of the original image mixed back

cards.equivalent: Lumetri Color Creative tint or Tint (Premiere)
cards.scripting: Colours are '#RRGGBB'. Blend With Original is animatable: keyframe 100 -> 0 to fade into the toned look. GPU support is from memory, not harvested.

cards.name: Vibrance

verified.note: Colours are visibly punchier than the untouched render (stripes, foreground-block reds and navy areas richer; mean saturation 0.15 -> 0.26) with faces still natural.

cards.summary: Raises (or lowers) the saturation of the least saturated colours more than already saturated ones, protecting skin tones; Saturation changes all colours equally.
use_for: make flat press/handout footage pop without orange faces
punchier colour for social reels
muted documentary look with negative Vibrance/Saturation
even out saturation between sources
avoid: Saturation above ~40 clips saffron/red flags and logos
boosting heavily compressed footage reveals chroma blocking

params.name: Vibrance
params.does: smart saturation that favours dull colours and spares skin

params.name: Saturation
params.does: uniform saturation for all colours

cards.scripting: Two plain numbers, -100..100, both animatable. GPU support is from memory, not harvested.

cards.name: Video Limiter

verified.note: Gamut Warning paints large out-of-range areas bright green (walls, faces, stripes, foreground-block tops), so Clip Level 1 is a strict level and the warning colour applies.

cards.summary: Clamps luma and chroma to a broadcast-legal level, optionally compressing values before the clip point; Gamut Warning paints out-of-range pixels in a warning colour.
use_for: final broadcast-safe pass on TV news deliveries
check which graphic colours exceed the legal range (Gamut Warning on)
tame super-white phone-footage highlights before a TV export
avoid: leaving Gamut Warning on at render burns the warning colour into the output
pointless for web/Instagram delivery and dulls highlights
placing it before other grading: effects after it push levels out again (keep it last, on a top adjustment layer)
stacking it with Broadcast Colors: double limiting, pick one

params.name: Clip Level
params.does: popup: the luma/chroma ceiling (1-4)

params.name: Compression before clipping
params.does: popup: soft-roll values toward the ceiling before hard clipping (1-5)
params.typical: 1 (default) or a middle entry for gentler highlights

params.name: Gamut Warning
params.does: checkbox: highlight illegal pixels instead of fixing them

params.name: Gamut Warning Color
params.does: colour used to flag illegal pixels

cards.scripting: All four properties are non-animatable (harvested): static values only. Clip Level and Compression before clipping are 1-based popups (read from After Effects 26.0): Clip Level 1 100 IRE (SMPTE range), 2 103 IRE (the default), 3 105 IRE (EBU R103 Preferred), 4 109 IRE (SDI limit); Compression 1 None, 2 3%, 3 5%, 4 10%, 5 20% (Clip Level 1 is the strict level: in the gallery render with Gamut Warning on it flagged walls, faces and stripes). On normal footage the effect is subtle; the demo uses Clip Level 1, the strongest compression and Gamut Warning on so affected highlights are painted green. Always send Gamut Warning 0 for a deliverable.

cards.name: Bezier Warp

verified.note: Frame edges are curved (top edge bowed, left edge pulled in) with black exposed around the warped image, a clear Bezier border warp.

cards.summary: Warps the layer by moving the 4 corner vertices and 8 tangent handles of a Bezier border, curving the edges (flag wave, page curl, bowed card).
use_for: wave a flag or banner graphic
curve a screenshot or newspaper-clipping card like held paper
fake screen curvature on a phone/TV-screen insert
fit a graphic onto a curved surface
avoid: extreme tangents fold the image over itself
on a full-frame layer the edges pull in and expose empty corners; use it on smaller cards or pre-scale
Quality below ~6 shows faceting

params.name: Top Left Vertex
params.does: top-left corner position
params.typical: near [0, 0]; move inwards a little for perspective

params.name: Top Left Tangent
params.does: handle shaping the left third of the top edge

params.name: Top Right Tangent
params.does: handle shaping the right third of the top edge
params.typical: [1280, -150..150] (opposite sign of the left tangent = S-wave)

params.name: Right Top Vertex
params.does: top-right corner position

params.name: Bottom Right Tangent
params.does: handle shaping the right third of the bottom edge

params.name: Bottom Left Tangent
params.does: handle shaping the left third of the bottom edge

params.name: Quality
params.does: mesh subdivision quality

cards.equivalent: Corner Pin (Premiere; straight edges only, no curves)
cards.scripting: Points are layer-space pixels; the defaults assume a 1920x1080 layer (vertices at corners, tangents at the thirds), so scale them for other layer sizes. Order runs clockwise: Top Left Vertex, Top Left Tangent, Top Right Tangent, Right Top Vertex, Right Top Tangent, Right Bottom Tangent, Bottom Right Vertex, Bottom Right Tangent, Bottom Left Tangent, Left Bottom Vertex, Left Bottom Tangent, Left Top Tangent. For a looping flag wave keyframe the tangents (or add sine expressions).

cards.name: Bulge

verified.note: A large fisheye magnification bump fills the frame centre (background at the centre blown up into a round swelling that pushes the stripes and dark areas outward).

cards.summary: Magnifies (positive height) or pinches (negative height) an elliptical area around a centre point, like a fisheye lens bump.
use_for: big-head / bulging-eyes gag in satire reels
magnifying-glass effect on a headline word, signature or document detail
pinch-punch transition on a beat
subtle bump on a punch-in for emphasis
avoid: on real people in straight news it reads as mockery or manipulation
small radius with high height tears pixels; use Antialiasing High for the final render

params.name: Horizontal Radius
params.does: width of the bulge area in pixels

params.name: Vertical Radius
params.does: height of the bulge area in pixels

params.name: Bulge Center
params.does: centre of the bulge (layer pixels)
params.typical: on the face or detail, e.g. [960, 540]

params.name: Bulge Height
params.does: strength; negative pinches

params.name: Taper Radius
params.does: edge fall-off: how steeply the bulge slopes at its rim (0 = default); subtle, exact direction unverified

params.name: Antialiasing (Best Qual Only)
params.does: edge smoothing at Best quality

params.name: Pinning
params.does: checkbox: keep the layer edges fixed

cards.equivalent: Spherize (Premiere; round magnify only, no pinch or separate radii)
cards.scripting: Bulge Center is in layer-space pixels; track it to a face with a null/expression if the subject moves. Radii are 0-8000 px; Bulge Height -4..4. Pinning is a 0/1 checkbox.

cards.name: CC Bend It

verified.note: Bend 20 now reads as a clean rubber-strip flex: a band about 690 px wide centred on the Start-End axis stays upright at the bottom and curves to lean right toward the top, faces/stripes/flowers readable, where the old Bend 80 curled it upside-down into an unreadable fan; the strip leaves ~65% of the frame black on both sides.

cards.summary: Bends the layer along the line from a Start point to an End point, like flexing a rubber strip; Render Prestart decides what happens to the part before Start.
use_for: wobble or bend a logo, title or cut-out sticker on a playful reel beat
sway a cut-out pole, flag-staff or mic stand
rubber-hose cartoon motion on explainer icons
avoid: full-frame footage: only a band around the Start-End axis is drawn (measured on frame 061: ~690 px wide for a 1080 px axis), so everything left and right of it goes black, about 65% of a 1920x1080 frame; use it on a cut-out element, not a full plate
Start/End must span the element or only part of it bends
Bend 80 on a full-height axis curls the layer past 90 degrees into an upside-down fan with most of the frame black

params.name: Bend
params.does: bend amount and direction (sign)
params.typical: 10-30 (either sign) on a full-height axis; 80 already curls the layer upside-down

params.name: Start
params.does: anchor end of the bend axis (layer pixels)

params.name: End
params.does: free end of the bend axis (layer pixels)

params.name: Render Prestart
params.does: popup: how the area before Start is drawn (1-4)

params.name: Distort
params.does: popup: distortion mode (1-2)

cards.equivalent: none in Premiere (closest: Wave Warp, Corner Pin)
cards.scripting: Start/End are layer-space pixels (defaults [960, 810] -> [960, 270] on a 1920x1080 layer); put them at the base and tip of the element. Render Prestart (1-4) and Distort (1-2) are popups; Render Prestart: 1 None, 2 Static, 3 Bend (default), 4 Mirror; Distort: 1 Legal, 2 Extended (read from After Effects 26.0). Bend is roughly the total curl angle along the Start-End span at about 1.8 degrees per unit: measured on gallery frame 061, Bend 80 bent a bottom-to-top axis into a ~145 degree arc curling to the right, so 20 is about 36 degrees. Animate Bend with keyframes or a wiggle/sine expression for a wobble. Only a band centred on the Start-End axis is rendered (measured on gallery frame 061: about 690 px wide for the 1080 px [960,1080]->[960,0] axis, with Render Prestart 3 and Distort 1); pixels outside that band are dropped, whether the width scales with axis length or changes with Distort 2 is unverified.

cards.name: CC Bender

verified.note: The layer leans and curves to the right toward the top (Top end swung over, black wedge exposed at the upper left), a clear bend about the Base-Top axis.

cards.summary: Bends the layer around the axis from Base to Top so it leans or curves; Style picks the bend shape.
use_for: make a cut-out character, icon or sticker lean and sway
cartoon bounce on explainer graphics
bendy text for comedic beats in satire reels
avoid: full-frame footage bends off-frame and exposes empty corners
Base/Top not covering the element leaves parts unbent

params.name: Amount
params.does: bend strength and direction (sign)

params.name: Style
params.does: popup: bend shape
params.typical: 1 Bend for smooth lean, 3 Sharp for a kink

params.name: Adjust To Distance
params.does: checkbox: scale the bend to the Base-Top distance

params.name: Top
params.does: tip of the bend axis (layer pixels)

params.name: Base
params.does: fixed base of the bend axis (layer pixels)

cards.equivalent: none in Premiere (closest: Wave Warp, Corner Pin)
cards.scripting: Top/Base are layer-space pixels (defaults [960, 270] / [960, 810] on a 1920x1080 layer). Style: 1 Bend, 2 Marilyn, 3 Sharp, 4 Boxer (read from After Effects 26.0). Adjust To Distance is a 0/1 checkbox. Keyframe Amount or drive it with a sine expression for a sway.
